answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph, with transition mass attenuated by each step. A Sybil cluster is an adversarial set S whose sparse external cut gives conductance φ(S)=cut(S,V∖S)/vol(S)≪1; only leakage through a trusted bridge or inlet can raise its stationary reach. Conductance and min-cut bounds therefore cap S’s aggregate voting weight, while a gale of internal attestations cannot amplify it beyond that leakage.
